_meta.purpose: Learning register for the AI PM content track. One topic per month, anchored at the 21st LinkedIn slot. Spec: analysis/distribution/DISTRIBUTION_SPEC.md §8.
_meta.admission_rule: No entry is marked published without at least one measurement carrying a value AND a source file. Prose alone does not qualify.
_meta.capture_rule: When any session produces a number that measures the active topic, append it to that topic's measurements[] before the session ends. The active topic is named in CLAUDE.md so it is always in context.

measurements.how_measured: analysis/signals/is_news.py --measure. Selector scores each L1 signal 2*record + 2*regime-flip + 1*crossed; a read must clear floor 2.0 (a strong factor). observations: The +9.99 pp incident (2026-07-21): an invented pair-divergence value PASSED the first negative test because the signal was classified scan-like, pooling a pp gap with two pct rates and deriving cumulative sums. Fixing the classification made the same corruption hard-fail. Lesson: a groundedness check is only as good as the ground-truth shape it compares against.
First newsletter traceability cut was vacuous — period-wide scope let invented numbers pass. Rescoping to declared signals only was the fix. Same lesson as Check 4f's evidence_all rescoping.
Negative testing must target the artifact the validator actually reads. The pair-divergence negative test only worked after editing analysis/rbi_atm_pos/insights.json rather than the web copy.

Loosening a gate can be invisible: the distribution gate initially inherited the card policy (abs_tol=0.25 plus ratio grounding) and passed every negative test I threw at it — not because the text was grounded but because a 29-value pool spawns ~800 candidate ratios and a quarter-point tolerance covers most of the number line worth inventing. Catch rate 41.5%. The same check, scoped to rounding width and with ratio grounding removed, catches 95.7%. A gate that never fails is not evidence of correctness; measure the catch rate.

Groundedness has two error rates, and only measuring one is how you ship a gate that blocks the truth. Tightening tolerance took false rejections from 0 to 3/25 until the formatting quirk behind them was fixed; both numbers belong in the measurement.

The gate guarding the subscriber-facing newsletter caught 0% of invented numbers, and had passed every hand-written negative test since it was built. Hand-written negative tests select for numbers the author already suspects; an injection harness does not. Every gate needs a measured catch rate before it can be described as working.

A defensive default is a hole. When per-block scoping was added, blocks with no declared signals fell back to the issue-wide pool 'so nothing breaks' — that single fallback dropped the in-range catch rate from 91.9% to 42.4%, because the injection site was exactly such a block. Removing the fallback took it to 99.5%. Scope defaults should fail closed.

Tightening surfaced two real bugs that the loose gate had been hiding, both display-format rather than data problems: values rendered for the reader (₹2.9L Cr, 12.0 crore) did not match their stored form, and ratio grounding had been silently accepting them as a/b of other values. The fix — ground the value through the same renderer the issue uses — is exact rather than a tolerance guess.

CORRECTION to the 2026-07-21 newsletter entries (100.0%/99.5% near-miss/in-range): those numbers measured decision point D2, not the gate. The old measure_groundedness.py:138 injected into the FIRST p block then broke; in the deep read that block is the signal-less intro, which grounds nothing and fails closed. All 200 injections hit one always-fail block. The blocks that can actually leak — basis lines scoped to thousands of values — were never attacked. This is the FOURTH appearance of the narrow-negative-test failure class (Check 4f period-wide -> newsletter v1 -> distribution -> the harness itself). Fixed 2026-07-23: inject every eligible block, report per decision point and per scope band, never one pooled number.

The honest newsletter picture after the fix: D1 in-range catch is 92.8% pooled but that pooling hides the real story — it is 100% up to ~200 candidate values and 79% beyond 1000. Scope width, not tolerance, is what a wide-scope gate leaks on. This is the empirical case for the deep-read D1 scope fix (basis lines -> member's own signal instead of the driver's whole evidence_all set): narrowing scope is expected to move those wide-band blocks from 79% back toward 100%.

Method lesson banked for the track: automating a negative test freezes the author's choice of injection SITE, not just their choice of value. A catch rate is only trustworthy sliced by the scope of the site attacked; a single artifact-level number is the same vacuity as a single period-wide ground-truth pool, one level up.

is-news selector design: the first cut flipped on ~50% of signals because status wobbles accelerating<->decelerating (strengthening<->active) every noisy month while still growing. Fixed by counting a flip only on a REGIME change (growing<->shrinking<->flat), not the within-regime wobble; the wobble is demoted to the weakest factor (crossed, weight 1) and can never make something a read alone. Second finding: labelling ALL share signals as templates was too coarse -- a share at an all-time reversal record (credit-cards' share of personal loans) is a legitimate read, not a template. The clean template is a share that ALSO didn't move.

Building the merged monthly issue surfaced 6 advice/forecast warnings in verbatim card prose (the is-news reads inherit LLM-eval consulting-speak: 'Lenders should allocate capital exclusively to UPI QR', 'the ratio will continue widening through FY27'). These are WARNINGS not failures by design (Sec 11.1 / Sec 5.3): card prose is the eval's, fixed upstream at prompt v1.12, never hand-edited in the renderer. The new prose_lint's advice+forecast detectors make that fix list visible for the first time -- 6 concrete card-prose items feeding v1.12.

is-news + magnitude factor (reco b): adding magnitude (>2x typical move, weight 2) surfaced large-corporate +14.4% YoY as a credit read it would have missed on record/regime alone. Trade-off measured: selectivity rose to 48.7% of signals clearing the read floor this cycle (a broad-growth month) -- the top-2 reads stay unambiguous but 'a read is the exception' weakens; tunable via MAGNITUDE_MULT. Template-reject held at 100%. Second note: the word-vs-number check had a false-positive class on legitimate 'fell 4.3%' prose (word carries the sign, magnitude is unsigned); fixed by firing only on EXPLICITLY-signed rates (the real 'up, -2.6%' bug), plus word-boundary cues so bare up/down fire without tripping on group/update.

Determinism-vs-judgment lesson (seeds topic #5): unit formatting is MECHANICAL and must not be an LLM job — v1.12's prose rule 'counts in lakh/crore, never millions' leaked badly (120.5M, 1.02M, 147K all over atm_pos) however firmly stated, because the model reliably reverts to M/K. Moving it to a deterministic post-pass (normalize_units at eval write) fixed it 100% by construction. Prose voice/advice/forecast, which IS judgment, correctly stayed a prompt fix. Also found: a prompt can defeat its own rule — v1.12 banned 'entrenched' on one line while the streak-type guide taught 'long streak = entrenched trend' on another; fixing the contradiction cut entrenched 7→1.

observations.note: Direction-render bug ('up, -2.6% YoY') fixed at the RIGHT layer: the render shows the OBSERVED value and tags a member '(moving against)' when its observed sign opposes its authored polarity — it never derives an up/down WORD from authored direction. word_number_conflicts hard-fails = 0 in generated deep-read text. Both tokens used to trace, so the number gate was structurally blind to it; the fix is a new agreement rule, not a tolerance change. This is the same class as the monthly issue's word-vs-number check — a defect can trace perfectly and still contradict itself.

The gate biting is the deliverable, not a regression. Attaching per-member signals cut the deep read's basis-line scope ~35x (2,258→65) with no measurable catch loss — evidence that the earlier wide-pool pass rate was partly vacuous breadth, the 4f/newsletter lesson recurring. Determinism-vs-judgment (AI PM #5) shows up structurally here too: Part A (banks) is fully computed, the spine is a machine-ranked shortlist the human picks — the same 'machine ranks, editor picks' seam as the monthly reads.

Prose is now a BUILD-ONCE-REUSE mechanism, not a deep-read patch (user steer): core/voice.py owns the voice (register/advice/forecast/units/direction) + conversational builders; the gate's prose_lint/word_number_conflicts delegate to it, so monthly issues, LinkedIn and the deep read ask their prose identical questions. The FY-range date leak ('2022-23' -> stray -23) resurfaced in the sourcing citation and was fixed at the presentation strip (the same class as Check 2g's FY22-24). Diagram design settled the user's 'representation not generation' point: the model already held the signed causal graph; the shallow triangle was a generation bug, not a model gap.

S4a live-fetch finding: the verification CHANNEL constrains the mechanism more than the allowlist. Anthropic's crawler (WebFetch, and the API web_search which shares the identity) is 403'd by PIB, NPCI, Business Standard; web.archive.org unreachable; Wikipedia fetched fine (tool works, sites block). The gate did the right thing — published NOTHING rather than an unverifiable claim. Resolution: verify the excerpt against page text from a channel the sites permit (the editor's logged-in Chrome via Claude-in-Chrome, or a paste); excerpt_on_page is agnostic to how the text was obtained. Not fabricating a 'verified' stamp and not spoofing a UA to evade bot blocks are both first-order honesty constraints here. The mechanism 'earns its place' precisely by refusing.

§5.3 lint EXPOSED the §14 upstream blocker as a hard gate: the 14th slot (C6/C7 openings/risks) hard-fails on raw floats (1358241.0 micro ATMs, 12.0 periods) that generate_opportunity_narrative leaks — the LLM is told to copy exact signal values verbatim so they trace under Check 4f, and 4f accepts only raw flat_numbers, not the lakh/crore reader form. So the fix chain is: 4f must accept as-rendered forms (like the distribution gate's _as_rendered), THEN the narrative can pass the LLM display values, THEN re-run the narrative LLM + regen feed. That is a core-gate + LLM-rerun change affecting /opportunities + deep read + slots — a distinct workstream from the LinkedIn §5 changes. 4/5 slots (1st/7th/28th pass, 21st skips by design) are clean; only C6/C7 is gated, correctly, on real debt.

Prompt instructions are necessary but not sufficient — the LLM emitted 'the bank should push...' on 3 cross-system items despite an explicit 'never say should'. The fix that held was the DETERMINISTIC guard (drop advice implications via core.voice), consistent with the platform's traceable-not-assumed principle: enforce in code, don't trust the model. Also a caching lesson: cross-system enrichment was narrative-flag-gated, so a preserved narrative:True blocked re-narration after the prompt change — switched it to cache-gated (like the pipeline path) so a cache clear forces a fresh run. Machine implications are now observations or empty; the prescriptive 'so what' is the editor's on every surface (/opportunities included).

open_questions: Breadth-based (period-wide) checks let an in-range invented number pass. What is the cheapest scoping that closes this for free prose, not just structured values?
Can groundedness be measured as a single rate across both pipelines, or is it inherently per-check?
